objective: Measure and repair the minutes-scale wallet-authority approval path without shrinking the full state-deepening soak, then establish enough repeated and mutation-tested release evidence to justify a per-approval latency tripwire.
falsifiable_claim: For a fixed backend and build profile, the profiling harness attributes each approval's wall and CPU time to submission, consensus/finalization, execution, state commitment, durable persistence, and proof/resolution while recording height, state/version depth, and bytes; incomplete attribution fails closed, and a numeric performance tripwire remains absent until repeated release-host evidence selects a budget and a planted delay defeats it.

code_anchors.must_contain: RESTART: all ten named lifecycles and auxiliary terms/eligibility evidence reproject exactly

adversarial_or_fault_proof: The complete pre-repair and post-repair release profiles each attributed all 27 approvals across 27 heights with zero anomalies, release/IAVL/Redb provenance, readiness lag 1, and exact depth/version buckets. Pre-repair AFT finalization grew from 1,503 to 31,056 ms over versions 74-215/depths 9-11 while IAVL commitment stayed 0.003-0.010 ms and persistence stayed 19.875-33.213 ms. Bounded admitted-anchor verification, unchanged-tip suppression, current-live-tip ingestion validation, and combined atomic IAVL commit reduced AFT finalization to 56-94 ms through version 919/depth 12; commitment remained 0.004-0.009 ms and persistence 25.920-36.228 ms. Restoring the warm full-prefix rewalk made the depth mutation fail; inverting the non-regressing-tip predicate made its focused mutation fail; the profiler's 21-test missing-field and attribution suite is fail-closed. Both full semantic runs remain exactly 14/15 on the final restarted OutcomeRoom dependency, after all nine child-family and auxiliary counts reprojected exactly. No latency tripwire is set because one host's pre/post runs do not yet select a reproducible budget or mutation-test that budget itself.
remaining_nonclaims: No numeric approval latency budget is established; repeated release-host baselines and a mutation of the selected budget are still required.
The repair attributes the dominant observed growth to repeated AFT canonical-collapse rewalks; it does not claim all latency is AFT or that IAVL, Redb, cryptography, replay, and polling have no cost.
Jellyfish is disqualified from a performance comparison until incremental commit, proof, persistence/restart, pruning, and historical-anchor parity are mechanized through the state abstraction.
Batching and fractal partitioning were not implemented: the first-order usage repair removed the measured dominant growth, and cross-partition adjudication would first have to fail closed.
The scheduled soak proves only the exact profile and environment it runs.
The release-profile baseline remains 14/15, not a green full-soak claim; the final restarted OutcomeRoom projection still lacks its owner-record runtime dependency.
M04.6 ownership, individual authority receipt semantics, the deterministic blocking lane, the full scheduled release soak, and M04.8's prior nonclaims remain unchanged.
source_provenance: Opened 2026-08-27 from M04.8 verifier evidence. On 2026-08-28, complete release/IAVL/Redb pre/post profiles attributed the defect to repeated steady-state AFT canonical-collapse rewalks, mutation-tested the bounded repair and live-tip ingestion guard, and retained the unchanged complete journey. ADR 0038 preserves the full semantic soak while separating it from the deterministic merge lane; the exact measurements and artifact hashes are registered in the M04.8 commit-path evidence file.
